item.title: Free government program to help 2,700 parents back to work could bring new enrolments
item.description: A family already using two days of early learning may need a third when a parent returns to work. For another family, accepting a job or starting a training course may mean enrolling a child for the first time. For services with vacancies, either change could help fill an available day.

item.title: New updated asthma guidance changes how children under five are diagnosed
item.description: New asthma guide for very young children has been updated which identifies that children can be assessed for asthma if they demonstrate wheezing and/or breathlessness whilst playing.The new guidelines from Therapeutic Guidelines provide information on how asthma can be diagnosed in young children based on their symptoms and a ‘test’ period of medication.

item.title: Are part-time rosters about to change: Fair Work reviews modern award
item.description: The Children’s Services Award 2010 is one of the eleven awards currently under investigation by The Fair Work Commission which is investigating part-time work and how that work can be altered.

item.title: Quality in early learning and care lives in relationships, not paperwork
item.description: Ask an experienced early childhood educator what quality looks like and they won’t start with a compliance checklist. They’ll tell you about the warmth and meaning of their relationships with children, families and colleagues. They’ll explain how a particular child needs a gentle start each week to slowly settle back in.

item.description: Children are often seen by educators and teachers to first watch and then participate in games that other children play. In some cases they can then act as ‘teachers’ and teach others how to play a game.
